name: Critique, feedback and revision rounds
one_line: REFUSED. A revision round is not an organizational situation: it is a version-family/group relationship inside one creative project or client engagement, linking what was shown, the feedback received, the variant made in response, and any approval. The same cycle occurs in research manuscripts, construction drawings, engineering designs, code review and ordinary office documents, so `_R2`, comments and approval language cannot activate a creative template. Coverage remains intact through universal `version_family` metadata, P9 grouping, the active project's template, and residual review for unattached feedback. The fieldless placeholder creative schema licenses no dimensions, and this row has no distinct privacy rule. Absorbs legacy `studio.revision-round` without rebuilding a relationship as a node.
refuse_reason: Fails all three node-test legs. (1) Detection: `_v3`, `_R2`, `FINAL`, comments, tracked changes, proof annotations and approval messages are real evidence of a universal version family or a file-neighborhood edge, but none is creative-specific. The design explicitly makes version family universal: “a small shared set of universal file facts, such as file type, creation date, language, duplicate family, version family, and sensitivity status.” A revision cycle requires multiple records and relations; it is not a per-file schema activation. The strongest creative evidence—a brief, named job, working-file structure or delivery set—activates the creative project or client engagement, not a round. (2) Dimensions: empty by contract because `creative` declares no fields. Even if `project`, `stage`, `artifact_type` and `client` are later adopted, round/revision is a `stage` value or accepted-group label beneath the project, not a new template. A round-first collector would scatter one work across `R1`, `R2`, and `R3`. (3) Privacy: comments may be candid and unreleased work may be confidential, but those rules attach to the containing engagement or project and apply equally to its brief, working files and handoff. No different posture exists. Therefore the row is neither the schema default nor a distinct template; it is graph structure plus values.

deterministic: None authored for template activation. A same-stem run of byte-different files with ordered version tokens is deterministic evidence for the universal `version_family` fact, not for this template or even for the creative schema.

A closed feedback cycle can be assembled only as P9 graph structure: a presented variant, a dated or threaded response that identifies it, a later variant whose changes answer that response, and an explicit acceptance or supersession record. That structure is useful and real, but graph edges carry file ids, never template ids; it therefore proves the refusal rather than saving the node.
needs_llm: matching free-prose comments to the exact variant they discuss when filenames, attachment names and quoted thumbnails disagree
deciding whether a later variant answers requested changes or is an independent alternative; this may support a reviewable edge but may not write causation as fact without explicit evidence
distinguishing approval of a concept, approval to proceed, approval of copy and final release approval when the message says only `looks good`
deciding whether several simultaneous variants are alternatives within one round or separate works
never_alone: `v2`, `rev B`, `R3`, `FINAL`, `approved`, `amends`, `comments`, `proof` or `feedback` in a filename; the same vocabulary occurs across research, legal, construction, engineering, code and office records
a comment count, tracked-changes stream, annotation layer or PDF sticky notes; these establish review activity but not creative activation
high text, pixel or layer similarity between files; similarity supports retrieval and version-family review but does not establish direction, round number or approval
filesystem creation or modification order; copies, exports and downloads can reverse the real review sequence
an email subject beginning `Re:` or a thread containing an attachment; thread membership is context, not proof that the message critiques that attachment
a client, reviewer, studio or brand name without a labelled role; an organisation can commission, author, review, supply or merely be mentioned
a `design_creative` source type or creative extension; extension is a routing signal, never meaning
membership in one folder named `Revisions`, `Feedback`, `WIP` or `Final`; a curated folder aids retrieval but does not create facts
a bounded download or export session; session proximity cannot establish a feedback-to-variant causal edge
the absence of an approval record; silence does not mean rejected, pending or abandoned

grouping_reasons: No template grouping authored. P9 may assemble one reviewable cycle from explicit attachment identity, quoted filenames, version-family membership, dated feedback, response notes and approval records without activating this row or copying facts between members.
A file may belong both to its project group and to a version family. Those overlapping memberships are the designed graph behavior, not evidence for another organizational template.

template.why: Empty because the row is refused and because the creative placeholder schema declares no fields. A revision-round level would be structurally wrong even after field adoption: one named work remains the intelligible parent, while round is a stage/group label within it. The user may browse a cycle in the graph without freezing `R1/R2/R3` as folders. Not time-first: sent time, comment time, export time, approval time and filesystem time are different observations.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone marked proof or versioned file with durable purpose but no recoverable project association belongs here rather than in a synthetic round collector. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

Unattached comments, ambiguous approvals and feedback messages whose target version cannot be resolved need a future decision. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

A photographed markup with no recoverable project association is an isolated image, not sufficient evidence for a revision situation. “One-Off Images may hold isolated image files that are neither screenshots nor members of a coherent photo event.”

Candid critique, unreleased work and named counterparties can require local-only handling even when no project can be resolved. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

sensitivity_why: Recorded so refusal does not drop protection. Feedback may contain candid assessments of named people, unreleased concepts, embargoed campaign details, client strategy and internal approval disputes. This posture belongs to the containing project or engagement and applies equally to the variants and handoff; it does not distinguish a revision-round template. No P7 handling class is assigned here.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: whether product UI should expose a named `revision cycle` view or typed graph edge family joining presented variant → feedback → responding variant → approval. Option (a), recommended here: derive a reviewable cycle from universal version_family facts and P9 evidence without adding a roster node or field. Option (b): add a universal graph relation vocabulary in a later graph decision, still not a creative template. Option (c): adopt `stage` on the creative schema and permit user-confirmed round labels as values. This row cannot choose among P9/P6 product changes and mints none.
